record.original_question: Which finite almost simple groups are the automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3? In other words, which finite almost simple groups are generated by three involutions two of which commute? This question has been answered for finite simple groups; see 7.30 in Archive. Ya.

evidence.quote: Which finite almost simple groups are the automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3? In other words, which finite almost simple groups are generated by three involutions two of which commute? This question has been answered for finite simple groups; see 7.30 in Archive. Ya.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite group $G$ is called almost simple if there exists a finite non-abelian simple group $S$ such that $S \trianglelefteq G \leq \mathrm{Aut}(S)$ (identifying $S$ with its image of inner automorphisms). An abstract regular polytope of rank $3$ is a regular polytope whose automorphism group is generated by three involutions $\rho_0, \rho_1, \rho_2$ satisfying the commuting condition $(\rho_0 \rho_2)^2 = 1$ (together with the standard intersection condition for string C-groups of rank 3).

Equivalently, the automorphism group of a regular polytope of rank $3$ is a group generated by three involutions, two of which commute.

Classify all finite almost simple groups $G$ that arise as the automorphism group of some abstract regular polytope of rank $3$; equivalently, determine all finite almost simple groups that can be generated by three involutions, two of which commute.
artifact.category_tag: finite almost simple groups and regular polytopes
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for finite simple groups (Kourovka 7.30, Mazurov) has been resolved through a series of works covering alternating, sporadic, and Lie-type cases. For almost simple groups, partial results exist: e.g., results on PSL(2,q) and PGL(2,q) (Leemans–Liebeck and others) show certain almost simple groups are or are not C-groups of rank 3, and atlases of regular polytopes for small almost simple groups have been compiled. A complete classification for all finite almost simple groups does not yet appear in the literature, so the problem appears to be partially solved.

status_evidence.title: C-groups of PSL(2,q) and PGL(2,q)
status_evidence.snippet: Determines almost simple groups with socle PSL(2,q) that are C-groups of rank 3.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification for almost simple groups with socle PSL(2,q).

status_evidence.title: Atlas of Polytopes for Small Almost Simple Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Atlas containing regular polytopes whose automorphism group is an almost simple group.
status_evidence.claim: Computational classification exists for small almost simple groups.

status_evidence.title: Commuting involutions in finite simple groups
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses Mazurov's question 7.30 for finite simple groups.
status_evidence.claim: The simple-group case (Kourovka 7.30) is treated; almost simple is the natural extension.
